contentHtml:
Seeking an opportunity to embark on your journey from Dubai but no guidance on how to start with an industry that pays the best?

The most popular areas for professionals are the UAE and several Gulf nations, including Dubai. The UAE’s economy is a business-booming economy, therefore, many job seekers feel attraction towards it.

Job applicants before starting their job search frequently have a crucial question regarding the average salary in Dubai. Keeping this in mind, it is essential to be aware of minimum wage in Dubai in accordance with the law. If you don’t discover the salary wages before starting your career then you will wait for long and get stuck in low wages. Let us help you on this!

In this article:

  • We will be giving you the insights and trends regarding what is the minimum wage in Dubai.
  • Employee’s primary concerns when it pertains to employment relate to the earnings paid out and the expense of living.
  • Employee’s primary concerns when it pertains to employment relate to the earnings paid out and the expense of living.
  • Positions requiring knowledge and competence are highly rewarded, while roles demanding fewer abilities receive less.

Factors affecting Salaries

Dubai is a popular destination for:

  • Dubai is a popular destination for:
  • Expatriates and
  • Entrepreneurs

The city offers:

  • A high standard of living
  • A diverse culture and
  • A booming economy

But how much can you expect to obtain regarding your average salary in Dubai? What are the factors that affect your minimum wage in Dubai?

The most important factors that determine your average salary in Dubai is the area of industry in which you are working. Highest-paying industries in Dubai are:

  • Finance
  • Engineering
  • IT
  • Healthcare and
  • Construction

The lowest-paying industries are:

  • Hospitality
  • Retail
  • Education and
  • Administration

Recent studies show that the:

  • The average salary for an entry-level employee in Dubai is 12,000 AED per month, while
  • The average salary for a senior-level employee is 35,000 AED per month

Graduates from:

  • American
  • British, and
  • Australian colleges make more money than others

By Industry Average Salaries

  • Finance and Accounting:

10,000 AED – 130,000 AED

  • Banking and Financial:

15,000 AED – 155,500 AED.

  • Digital:

10,000 AED – 90,000 AED

  • Technology:

The expariates who indulge themselves in the IT industry have capable to earn 10,000 AED for support staff to 130,000 AED for chief IT officers.

  • Oil and Gas:

32,000 AED – 48,000 AED.

  • Engineering:

9,000 AED – 122,000 AED.

  • Education:

Those who are realated to educational department have a potential to earn 5,000 AED to 84,000 AED.

  • Hospitality and Tourism:

4,800 AED – 62,000 AED.

Salary Negotiation

  • Do your research: Do some research on the average salary for your position and industry in Dubai before going for an interview.
  • Highlight your achievements: Highlight your achievements that demonstrate your value and skills when discussing your salary.
  • Be flexible: Be flexible and open to negotiation, you should have a salary range in mind.
  • Be polite and professional: Be polite and professional throughout the negotiation process.

Comparison on Cost of Living

Minimum wage in Dubai

Housing:

  •  In a normal area, a furnished 85 m2 apartment rent is 7,073 AED.
  •  In a normal area, a furnished 85 m2 apartment rent is 7,073 AED.
  • In Abu Dhabi, the average monthly rent for a similar apartment in an expensive area is 8,500 AED
  • While in a normal area, it is 6,500 AED.

Food:

  • The average cost of a basic lunchtime menu (including a drink) in the business district of Dubai is 41 AED, while
  • A combo meal in a fast food restaurant is 32 AED.
  • A kilogram (2 lb.) of tomatoes costs 4.88 AED ($1.33), while
  • A kilogram (2 lb.) of tomatoes costs 4.88 AED ($1.33), while

Transportation:

  • The average cost of a one-way ticket on local transport in Dubai is 7.50 AED, while
  • A monthly pass costs 300 AED.
  • A liter (1/4 gallon) of gas costs 2.29 AED, while
  • A new Volkswagen Golf 1.4 TSI 150 CV (or equivalent) costs 90,230 AED.

Utilities:

  • The average cost of basic utilities for an 85 m2 apartment in Dubai is 893 AED, while
  • The average cost of internet is 330 AED.
  • In Abu Dhabi, the average cost of basic utilities for a similar apartment is 800 AED, while
  • The average cost of internet is 350 AED.

Latest salary trends

  • The guide predicts that wages in the UAE will increase by just under 2% in 2023.
  • Salaries in the UAE still remain higher than those in the UK, Europe, and Australia
  • Also, these regions offer other benefits such as tax-free income and a high quality of life.
  • These studies on minimum wage in Dubai also reveal that more than half of the UAE-based organizations surveyed (55%) grew their workforce in 2022.
  • Similarly, 59% plan to increase their headcount in 2023.
  • The most in-demand sectors are aviation and tourism, which have outperformed market expectations throughout 2022.

Summary

Engaging in a profitable industry will offer you a place where you want to be as Dubai has a pool of opportunities for the one who wants to work and get the best benefit out of it. As not every industry is offering good wages, so before starting your career it is essential for you to research and get the necessary skills or education to conquer the treasure.

Some of the individuals working in the industries like, IT, Banking institutions and Engineers can earn more than the rest. Similarly, educational background from prestigious institutions and developed countries also help you to get the best job that you desire!
